chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkinnarrated to us (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, who said: al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sadir al-Sayrafi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The light of Fatimah (peace be upon her) was created before the creation of the earth and the sky.' Some people said: 'O Prophet of Allah, is she not a human being?' He (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Fatimah is a heavenly, human being.' It was asked: 'O Prophet of Allah, how is she a heavenly, human being?' He said: 'Allah, the Almighty, created her from His light before He created Adam, when the souls were [created]. When Allah, the Almighty, created Adam, she was presented to Adam.' It was asked: 'O Prophet of Allah, where was Fatimah at that time?' He said: 'She was in her place beneath the leg of the Throne.' They asked: 'O Prophet of Allah, what was her sustenance?' He said: 'Glorification (Tasbih), Praise (Tahlil), and Exaltation (Tahmid).'

When Allah, the Almighty, created Adam and took me out from his loins, Allah loved to bring her out from my loins, so He made her a fruit (apple) in Paradise. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me with it and said to me: 'Peace be upon you and the mercy and blessings of Allah, O Muhammad.' I said: 'And upon you be peace and the mercy of Allah, my beloved Gabriel.' He said: 'O Muhammad, your Lord sends you greetings.' I said: 'From Him is peace, and to Him returns peace.' He said: 'O Muhammad, this is a fruit that Allah, the Almighty, has sent to you from Paradise.' So I took it and pressed it to my chest. He said: 'O Muhammad, Allah, the Majestic, says: Eat it all.' So I split it, and I saw a radiant light, and I was startled by it. He said: 'O Muhammad, why do you not eat? Eat it all and do not be afraid, for that light is Al-Mansurah in the heavens, and she on earth is Fatimah.'

I said: 'My beloved Gabriel, why is she called 'Al-Mansurah' in the heavens and 'Fatimah' on earth?' He said: 'She is called 'Fatimah' on earth because she separates (fattama) her followers from the Fire, and separates her enemies from her love. And she in the heavens is 'Al-Mansurah,' and that is the saying of Allah, the Almighty: "On that day, the believers will rejoice in Allah's victory. He grants victory to whom He wills." Meaning the victory of Fatimah for her lovers.'

key_terms.الْمَنْصُورَةُ: Al-Mansurah (The Victorious), a title for Fatimah in the heavens
key_terms.تَحْتَ سَاقِ الْعَرْشِ: Beneath the leg of the Throne, indicating her pre-Adamite location
key_terms.حُورَاءُ إِنْسِيَّةٌ: Heavenly human being, a title denoting her unique nature
key_terms.فَطَمَتْ شِيعَتَهَا: She separated her followers, referring to her role in salvation
key_terms.نُورُ فَاطِمَةَ: The light of Fatimah, referring to her spiritual essence

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Fatimah's creation from divine light before Adam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* underscores the Shia doctrine of *Nur al-Zahra*, positing that Fatimah’s essence was pre-existent and intimately linked to the Prophet’s own creation, thereby validating her unique spiritual authority. The narrative of her presentation as a 'fruit' containing radiant light serves as a metaphor for her role as the intercessor and the ultimate victory (*Nasr*) for her devotees, a concept the text explicitly links to divine promise. The etymological explanation of her name highlights her dual function in eschatology: separating her *Shi'a* from Hellfire while detaching her enemies from her love.
